solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Barge constructed by firm in the West Country

indicators.note: the firm's letters sit in the middle of the region's abbreviation

parts.note: SW is the abbreviation for the South West, England's West Country
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A canal boat built by a company based in Devon or Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Country is south-west England (Devon, Cornwall, Somerset), abbreviated SW.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed boat used for carrying freight, a kind of barge.

clue.text: Note taken originally during needlework

indicators.note: the letter comes in the course of, so inside, the needlework word

parts.note: crochet is needlework done with a hooked needle

indicators.note: the original letter of a word is its first one

parts.note: T is the first letter of taken

explanation.surface: Someone makes a note of something while doing their sewing.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet is a musical note, a quarter note in American usage.

clue.text: Upset writer cut sibling's son

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument, a writer
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: An upset author cut off a nephew from the will, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Your nephew is the son of your brother or sister.

clue.text: Hard work, introducing a new catchphrase

indicators.note: the hard work comes first and leads in the letters that follow

parts.note: a slog is a long spell of hard work

explanation.surface: Effort brings in a fresh motto, as for a campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a short memorable phrase used in advertising or politics, a catchphrase.

clue.text: Stalwart Republican in reading room

indicators.note: the party letter goes inside the room word

parts.note: a study is a room for reading and work

explanation.surface: A loyal party supporter sits in a library reading room.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalwart and sturdy both describe something strongly built and robust.

clue.text: Reported ages, yours and mine

indicators.note: reported means as spoken, signalling a word that sounds like another

parts.note: ages, as in 'it took ages', means hours

explanation.surface: Someone's age, as declared, belongs to the two of us.
explanation.walkthrough: HOURS with its silent H is said the same as OURS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ours is the possessive pronoun covering what belongs to you and me together.

clue.text: A North American attracting the old woman's curse

indicators.note: the first pieces draw the rest on after them

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, the old woman; the 's is 'is' joining to the definition

explanation.surface: An American draws down the wrath of an elderly lady.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is a formal ecclesiastical curse, or something vehemently detested.

clue.text: Most frightening way to arrest tooth decay

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold, so the street letters hold the decay word inside them

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
caries is the medical word for tooth decay

explanation.surface: A dentist's terrifying method of stopping cavities from spreading.
explanation.definitionFit: Scariest is the superlative of scary, meaning causing the greatest fear.

clue.text: A French coin in Brazil? That's illusory

parts.note: un is the French for a
the real is the currency of Brazil

explanation.surface: A French coin turning up in Brazil seems too unlikely to be true.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unreal is imaginary, existing only as an illusion.

clue.text: Nervous type in a hide, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who twitches with nerves
second meaning: a birdwatcher, who often watches from a hide

explanation.walkthrough: A hide is a camouflaged shelter for watching birds, not an animal skin; a twitcher is a keen birdwatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Twitcher is British slang for an obsessive birdwatcher and also describes a jumpy, twitching person.

clue.text: Course prepared by woman with second husband

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A meal course made by a woman and her new spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is a prepared item of food served as part of a meal, a course.

clue.text: Rise, lest soldiers get captured

indicators.note: the soldiers are captured, held inside the other phrase

parts.note: lest means in case
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: An alarmed general orders an uprising in case his troops are taken prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A rise and an increase are both a growth in amount or level.

clue.text: Manner in which food initially reaches a traveller

parts.note: a way is a manner of doing something
fare is food and drink provided

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: R is the first letter of reaches

explanation.surface: How a meal gets to someone on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayfarer is someone travelling on foot, a traveller.

clue.text: Woman identified by a US attorney

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, a US public prosecutor

explanation.surface: A woman picked out in a line-up by an American prosecutor.
explanation.definitionFit: Ada is a woman's given name, as in the mathematician Ada Lovelace.

clue.text: A Latina's working guard dog, perhaps

indicators.note: the letters are set to work, reorganised into a new order

explanation.surface: A Latin American woman's dog is on duty guarding the property.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alsatian, or German shepherd, is a breed often used as a guard dog.

clue.text: Glaswegian, possibly, most involved in survey

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the survey word

parts.note: to scan is to survey or look over

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A Glasgow resident features most heavily in an opinion poll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most' looks like part of the surface's 'most involved', but it is the fodder. Glasgow is Scotland's largest city.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Glasgow is an example of a Scot, hence the question-like 'possibly'.

clue.text: Test the writer's reason for action

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British vehicles
the writer refers to the setter, so the writer's (has) is I've

explanation.surface: An author explains why they're testing something.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is a compulsory yearly safety test for cars in Britain, named after the Ministry of Transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A motive is what prompts a person to act, the reason behind an action.

clue.text: Provoke pointer, say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to annoy or goad
second meaning: a ... on a dial or compass points to a value

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to irritate someone; as a noun it is the indicating arm on a gauge.

clue.text: Fish caught in unhappy setting

indicators.note: the letter for caught goes in the sad word
the unhappy word forms the setting around the letter, like a stone's mount

parts.note: sad means unhappy
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A fish is landed amid gloomy surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: The scad is a type of marine fish, also known as horse mackerel.

clue.text: Stripy insect used to be pest at first

parts.note: was is the past tense of be

indicators.note: at first selects the opening letter of the word

parts.note: P is the first letter of pest

explanation.surface: A striped bug was once considered a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: The wasp is a stinging insect with yellow and black stripes.

clue.text: Travelled in formal wear for a decade

indicators.note: the travelling word sits inside the clothing word

parts.note: ties are worn with formal clothing
went is the past of go, travelled

explanation.surface: Someone spent ten years travelling in a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: The twenties are the ten-year span from twenty to twenty-nine, as in the 1920s.

clue.text: Deserve attention finally given

parts.note: to give an ear is to pay attention

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the next word

parts.note: N is the last letter of given

explanation.surface: Someone deserves to be listened to at last.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn something is to merit or deserve it by effort.

clue.text: Expedition at a distance, in small island

indicators.note: the distance word sits inside the two letters

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
afar means at a distance

explanation.surface: A trip seen from far off on a tiny island.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an overland expedition, especially to observe wild animals in Africa.

clue.text: French writer, unexpected rival to Racine, ultimately

indicators.note: unexpected means arranged in a surprising way, so the letters are reshuffled
ultimately points to the last letter of the word

parts.note: E is the last letter of Racine

explanation.surface: A French author emerges as a surprise competitor to the dramatist Racine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpected' turns RIVALTO into VOLTAIR; 'ultimately' adds E, Racine's last letter. Racine was a French tragedian, a plausible rival.
explanation.definitionFit: Voltaire was the 18th-century French philosopher and author of Candide.

clue.text: Tiny bird in tear-jerking film

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small, tiny
pie is an old name for the magpie

explanation.surface: A small bird features in a sentimental movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A weepie is an informal term for a sad, sentimental film designed to make audiences cry.
